register.name: Treasury bills and bonds on the UMOA-Titres regional market
register.detail: State of Guinea-Bissau, through UMOA-Titres · auction of 6 July 2026, value date 7 July 2026 · 364-day bills due 5 July 2027 and 3-year bonds due 7 July 2029, coupon 6.25% · bids of FCFA 52.59bn, 420.75% of the amount offered
register.note: Weighted average yields of 5.94% on the bills and 7.97% on the bonds
register.text: The State of Guinea-Bissau raised FCFA 12.5 billion by auction of Treasury bills and bonds on the regional securities market of the West African Economic and Monetary Union, run by UMOA-Titres. Investors bid FCFA 52.59 billion, more than four times the amount offered. It is the sovereign’s own borrowing, in CFA francs, for the State budget.

register.name: Adaptation of agricultural production systems in coastal areas of northwest Guinea-Bissau (SAP025)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · grant · approved 20 October 2022 (B.34) · effective 15 September 2023 · 42% disbursed, latest disbursement 24 June 2026 · completion expected 15 September 2028
register.note: More than 200,000 vulnerable people expected to benefit
register.text: A Green Climate Fund grant of US$9.8 million, with the Sahara and Sahel Observatory as accredited entity, that rehabilitates small-scale water management schemes such as rainwater retention and irrigation, restores mangroves on 250 hectares of mangrove swamp and strengthens farm value chains with microenterprises. It serves the food and water standards in the coastal farming areas of the northwest.

register.name: Extended Credit Facility
register.detail: IMF · approved 30 January 2023 · access augmented 29 November 2023 · extended through 29 December 2026 · eleventh review completed 12 June 2026
register.note: Disbursed to June 2026: SDR 38.59 million, of which SDR 1.18 million on the eleventh review
register.text: A three-year IMF arrangement approved in January 2023 and extended in March 2026 through 29 December 2026, with access rephased in March 2026 to support implementation of the 2026 budget. Disbursements reached SDR 38.59 million (about US$54.8 million) with the eleventh review, completed on 12 June 2026. Outstanding IMF credit stood at SDR 56.27 million on 31 March 2026.

register.name: Rural Transport Project
register.detail: World Bank · US$15 million credit · implemented 2019 to 2025 · Ingoré to Ponte Caur main road and eight rural roads, Oio and Cacheu · completion reported 28 June 2025
register.note: About 30,000 residents of the northern regions expected to benefit
register.text: A World Bank credit of US$15 million, implemented from 2019 to 2025, that rehabilitated the Ingoré to Ponte Caur main road and eight rural roads in the northern regions of Oio and Cacheu. Rehabilitated roads serve the livelihood standard through access to markets and services.

register.name: Enhancing Connectivity in Northern Guinea-Bissau Project
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · commitment approved 25 June 2025 · P176948
register.note: The commitment shown for the project on World Bank Finances One
register.text: A World Bank commitment of US$14.7 million, approved on 25 June 2025, for transport connectivity in the north of the country. It serves the livelihood standard through access to markets and services.

register.name: Reform Advancement Development Policy Financing
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · grant · approved 1 May 2025, announced 2 May 2025 · P500567
register.note: Budget support tied to reforms of public finances, utilities and digital services
register.text: A US$10 million IDA grant of budget support for reforms of public financial management and domestic revenue, including the VAT law and a Treasury Single Account, and for the viability of electricity and water services and digital growth. Its expected results include lower electricity costs, lower internet costs and more fiscal space for education, health and social protection.

register.name: First digital census, additional financing (HISWACA)
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · grant · approved 31 March 2025 · Harmonizing and Improving Statistics in West and Central Africa, P178497 · census financing brought to US$10 million
register.note: Covers a cost overrun in carrying out the census
register.text: An additional IDA grant of US$4 million for Guinea-Bissau’s first fully digital census, the first census since 2009, under a regional statistics project that provides US$19 million for the country’s statistical capacity. A census counts the people whom each of the seven standards must reach.

register.name: Human Capital Project
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · grant · approved January 2025, announced 15 January 2025 · P179509
register.note: Cash transfers to poor and vulnerable families and an expanded National Social Registry
register.text: A US$20 million IDA grant to strengthen health, education and social services, with cash transfers to poor and vulnerable families, an expanded National Social Registry, a national community health strategy and new learning materials for schools. It is expected to benefit 111,000 primary school children, more than 200,000 pregnant women and adolescent girls and more than one million children under five.

register.name: Solar Energy Scale-up and Access Project
register.detail: World Bank · IDA grant $35M, Green Climate Fund $10.5M, ESMAP $2.65M · approved 28 May 2024 · financing agreement E3330-GW signed 10 June 2024 · P174576
register.note: Utility-scale solar parks and an upgraded and expanded grid
register.text: Solar generation and grid financing of US$48.15 million: a US$35 million IDA grant, US$10.5 million from the Green Climate Fund and US$2.65 million from ESMAP, for utility-scale solar parks, an upgraded and expanded grid, and support to the Ministry of Energy and the national utility, EAGB. It serves the energy standard, the one furthest from reach.

register.name: Public Administration and Public Finance Reform Programme, phase I
register.detail: African Development Bank · grant from the Transition Support Facility · approved by the Board 31 October 2024
register.note: Domestic revenue, control of public spending and transparency in public finances
register.text: A US$6.75 million grant from the African Development Bank’s Transition Support Facility, a window for states in transition, for the first phase of reforms of the public administration and public finances. It aims to raise domestic revenue, tighten control of public spending and strengthen oversight and transparency in the management of public money, which pays for public services.
